Source: (Slice comparison) in Part 0 of the supplied proof of dph_smooth_homotopy, using the dt-slice families (R4) and the locality (F2′). Siblings used: slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm) and locality (iwl_cr_ce_apply_eq_of_eqOn_nhds_support).

Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). For s ∈ ℝ let j_s(x) := cons(s, x).

1. (Coordinate identities.) For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x. Indeed EuclideanSpace.equiv applied to (EuclideanSpace.equiv).symm f returns f (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply); then (Fin.cons s g) 0 = s (Fin.cons_zero) and Fin.tail (Fin.cons s g) = g (Fin.tail_cons); finally (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) = x (ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply). Consequently, if s ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ spt X, then cons(s, x) ∈ cyl(spt X).
2. (Slice families.) Apply slice_forms (with P := m and m := q) to η and to η′. This gives φ, φ′ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) and φ′(s)(x)(v) = η′(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m. (The joint continuity also provided by slice_forms is not needed.)
3. (Product characterization.) The identities of step 2 hold in particular for s ∈ [0,1], so ProdChar(X, Z) applied to (η, φ) and to (η′, φ′) gives Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds and Z(η′) = ∫_0^1 X(φ′(s)) ds.
4. (The integrands agree on [0,1].) Fix s ∈ [0,1].
   (a) j_s is continuous: x ↦ Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) is continuous (a constant first entry and a continuous linear map; Continuous.finCons), and (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm is a continuous linear equivalence. Hence N_s := j_s⁻¹(N) is open.
   (b) spt X ⊆ N_s: for x ∈ spt X, cons(s, x) ∈ cyl(spt X) ⊆ N by step 1 and the hypothesis cyl(spt X) ⊆ N.
   (c) For x ∈ N_s the point y := cons(s, x) lies in N, so η(y) = η′(y). Hence for every v, φ(s)(x)(v) = η(y)(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) = η′(y)(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) = φ′(s)(x)(v), i.e. φ(s)(x) = φ′(s)(x) (extensionality of continuous alternating maps).
   (d) locality, applied with P := m, n := q, U := univ, T := X, ψ := φ(s), φ := φ′(s) and the open set N_s ⊇ spt X, gives X(φ(s)) = X(φ′(s)).
5. (Conclusion.) The functions s ↦ X(φ(s)) and s ↦ X(φ′(s)) agree on [0,1] = uIcc 0 1 (Set.uIcc_of_le), so intervalIntegral.integral_congr gives ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 X(φ′(s)) ds; no integrability is needed. By step 3, Z(η) = Z(η′). ∎
key_steps: slice_forms gives dt-slice families φ, φ′ of η, η′, and ProdChar gives Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds and Z(η′) = ∫_0^1 X(φ′_s) ds.
For s ∈ [0,1], j_s⁻¹(N) is open and contains spt X, because t(cons(s,x)) = s and tl(cons(s,x)) = x put cons(s,x) in cyl(spt X) ⊆ N.
φ_s = φ′_s on j_s⁻¹(N) since η = η′ on N, so locality gives X(φ_s) = X(φ′_s).
intervalIntegral.integral_congr on uIcc 0 1 = [0,1] gives Z(η) = Z(η′).
